root_idea.summary: The root centers on two attested orientations: destruction, ruin, or disabling stagnation, and testing or examination.
root_idea.development: The destruction branch extends from extreme stagnation to فساد and ruin, while the testing branch is concretely illustrated by bringing a she-camel to a stallion to determine pregnancy and then extends to examining or assaying something.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form بَارَ rather than the imperfect QAC lemma يَبُورُ.
Displayed as the independent verbal noun بَوَار.
Displayed as the adjective or verbal-noun epithet بُور.

senses.definition: To perish, be ruined, or prove vain and ineffectual.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the verb describes a thing, work, enterprise, or plan coming to ruin or failing; the negative construction in 35:29 expresses not perishing.

senses.definition: Destruction, perdition, or ruin resulting from utter stagnation.
senses.usage_conditions: An abstract noun; in دار البوار it denotes an abode of destruction or perdition.

senses.definition: Ruined, perishing, or in a state of perdition.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic constructions, it describes people as ruined or perishing. The form can function as an epithet for singular or plural and is not a separate sense merely because its grammatical number or gender varies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uncultivated, unsown, or fallow land; land left unplanted or in a bad agricultural state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of land, including land left fallow to be sown later.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become unsaleable or difficult to sell; of a market, to become stagnant in trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A commercial and market construction derived from the idea of uselessness through neglect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman without a husband, to remain undesired or undemanded in marriage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction describing prolonged failure to receive a marriage proposal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad or corrupt, destitute of good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical adjectival use, especially of a person, distinct from the Quranic description of being ruined or in perdition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deficiency, detriment, or a defective state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the collocation حُورٌ وَبُورٌ and related expressions of loss or impaired condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Erring, failing to apply oneself rightly, or not following right direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially attested in the collocation رَجُلٌ حَائِرٌ بَائِرٌ; the lexical relation is reported in connection with either sluggishness, perdition, or imitative pairing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring a she-camel to a stallion to determine whether she is pregnant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The test involves the stallion smelling the female; the construction is specialized to determining whether she is pregnant or not.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To try, assay, prove by experience, or examine someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May involve examining what is in a person's mind or discovering the state of a matter through testing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stallion-camel able to determine whether a female is pregnant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for the knowledgeable stallion in the pregnancy-testing construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone or something to perish; to destroy.
A destructive person who acts excessively in destroying others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agentive or personal description of destructive conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assert truthfully that one has had sexual intercourse with a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized derived-form use reported in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have sexual intercourse with a woman by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction referring to forcible intercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To charge or upbraid a person with something that is not in him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized derived-form use concerning a false attribution or accusation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woven reed mat, especially a rough mat or حصير.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized nominal usage; the plural is بَوَارِيّ.
A separately reported Arabicized usage, given as a synonym of طَرِيق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fish, especially a species of mullet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained as deriving from the Egyptian town بُورَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of reed mats of the بَارِيّ kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun derived from the mat term.

cautions: بُور has competing Classical analyses: it may be treated as a plural or quasi-plural of بَائِر, or as a verbal-noun epithet applicable across number and gender; these analyses do not require separate Quranic senses.

The derived-form discussion associated with the testing and sexual-conduct material transmits variant spellings, including اِبْتَوَرَ and ابتار; the specialized meanings are retained under the normalized headword اِبْتَوَرَ. The contrasting form ابتهر is not assigned to this root.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane passage in lane-unit:bwr:37436:g2:sub3 mixes the normalized form اِبْتَوَرَ with variant transcriptions ابتار and discusses a contrast with ابتهر. The meanings assigned to اِبْتَوَرَ are supported by the passage, but the exact orthographic transmission of the derived form remains uncertain.
